answer: To enter the earning set, an agent must first berth at a public registration wharf and lock a refundable bond that only unlocks after many epochs of accepted work. The bond is priced like cutting shale: each extra identity funded from the same source costs more than the last, so a farm's locked capital grows faster than any reward it can claim. If clustering or failed deliveries expose the group, every locked bond is slashed together. The fable that minting cheap names multiplies income fails once the rising lock, the delay, and joint slashing are enforced.
